justification: Carrying span: 'The river below it is thick with dace; one afternoon's netting last May took four hundred-odd of them, more than the trap has held in fifteen years', set against the book's own tally of 31 dace. A killed on 'Since the pass opened in 2011 the trap has been emptied most mornings of the run, the counts written into a hardbacked book' - the book begins in 2011; 1931 is only when the mill stopped, and the weir merely 'held water for' that mill. C killed for want of any span: 'The first nine springs are in one hand, the rest in three others' is about handwriting, not misidentification. D inverted by that same span - one hand did the first nine, three others the rest.

Carrying span: 'Of 74 tagged, 61 reached the weir, 54 on the left, and 39 went into the pass... Twelve came out at the top' - 27 of 39 failed, i.e. most. A killed on 'Of the eleven that entered above ten degrees, seven got out; of the twenty-eight that entered colder, five did' (roughly 64 per cent against 18). B killed on 'The pools do not help. They are short, and at April flows the jet from one notch reaches the wall of the next; there is no quiet corner in them.' C killed on 'A grayling is deep through the body and carries a dorsal fin like a sail' - the stated obstacle is build, and raw strength has already been set aside earlier in the piece.

Carrying span: 'They don't find it, and they don't find it because they don't come up that side of the river', with the too-little-flow half supplied by 'The pass releases about a quarter of a cubic metre a second; in April the river brings down nine. Four metres out from the mouth there is nothing of that quarter left to follow.' B killed on 'thinks strength has little to do with it', which is the passage explicitly discarding the fall-height account. C killed for want of any span - the trap is emptied 'most mornings of the run' and no seasonal opening date is given. D killed on 'Nine went in. Five came out at the top' - dace do enter individually, so no refusal to leave the shoal is on offer.

Carrying span: 'The other, three walls further up, came through the same water clear' - the passage holds the water constant and varies only position, so the implication carried is positional. A killed by that same 'the same water' clause: an identical spate did not pack the upper orifice, so the spate's force cannot be what singles out the lower one. B killed on the stated purpose, 'so a fish could go through a wall instead of over it'. D killed on 'two of the nine cross-walls were cut' plus 'it is still packed' - seven walls are uncut and one of the two cut ones is blocked.

The spine is three species with three outcomes and two distinct causes: trout, of which 'a trout goes up without appearing to try'; dace, who 'don't find it... because they don't come up that side of the river'; grayling, who enter 'as a fish that lives in the current would' but of whom 'Whatever stops them is inside.' A killed because the river above the weir is never discussed. B inverted by 'Nobody says the pass does not work. What has taken fifteen years to become interesting is what it works for' - the counts are the thing interrogated, not evidence marshalled for a thesis about throughput. C killed on proportion: the 2023 orifices occupy the closing three sentences, not the argument.

Carrying span: 'Where the glue went in, the sheet's gone like greased paper; you can read the back through it.' A killed on 'The rubber in it has oxidised - that's the brown', with the plasticiser assigned a different fate, 'has soaked into the paper'. B inverted on 'She warms a mend from last year, and the film lifts and brings most of the glue with it. On a mend as old as this one, heat does nothing. The glue has gone hard, she says, so only a solvent will move it.' D killed on 'The brown that's in the fibres I can lighten. I don't promise to take it out.' Interleave check: the narration beat 'She turns the certificate to the light.' now sits between the two halves of the quoted speech in paragraph 2, but it falls before the carrying clause and does not separate it from its subject; the key remains fully answerable from the paragraph as printed.

Carrying arithmetic, all of it on the page: 'Torget rymmer femtioåtta stånd', 'Alla som vill ha plats måste söka varje år', 'Fyra platser blev lediga inför förra höstens marknad', 'Sjuttiofyra sökte plats till den marknaden, och alla femtioåtta stånd var upptagna när den öppnade'. Route one: 74 applicants minus 58 filled stalls = 16 unplaced. Route two: 58 minus the 4 vacancies = 54 incumbents renewing, so 74 minus 54 = 20 new applicants competing for 4 places = 16 unplaced. Both routes give 16, and the reference class is unambiguous precisely because 'Alla som vill ha plats måste söka varje år' puts the incumbents inside the 74 rather than beside it. A killed on 'den som stod på torget året innan får stå där igen' - incumbency, not lot. B killed on 'står i Gottfrid Runessons namn och har gjort det längre än platskartan går tillbaka'. C inverted by that same incumbency clause.

Carrying span: the coda 'Flytta hela marknaden, båda dagarna, från och med nästa höst', with the tolerance half supplied by 'De första åren blir sämre. Ingen som räknar kommer fram till något annat, och jag skriver inte under på att det ordnar sig av sig självt.' B killed on 'båda dagarna' in that same coda. C killed on 'Jag var en av de tolv och har alltså inte torghandlarna bakom mig' - she concedes the majority's reasons hold but does not adopt their conclusion. D killed on 'Ett provår vill jag ändå inte ha.'

Carrying span: 'Vem som fick komma in avgjordes inte av hur nära man stod varandra, utan av vad besöket gällde. Prästen släpptes in, och distriktssköterskan, och karlen som skulle värdera skogen. De kom i ärenden som rörde hushållet.' B killed on 'Den som stod hushållet närmast kom sällan längre än till köksbordet' and 'Grannar och släkt satt i köket, oavsett hur långt de hade rest'. C killed on 'Sköterskan var oanmäld varannan gång och visades in ändå.' D killed on the same opening clause, which names errand and expressly denies closeness as the criterion; the esteem reading also has to survive 'Lars Uddén i huset intill blev stående i farstun med mössan i handen', and does not.

Carrying span: 'Sen bar far ut den i köket, för där gick spisen ändå', with 'Dörren till finrummet gick igen som förut' confirming that the watching left the room with the apparatus. A killed on 'Hemma hos oss stod farfars kista i finrummet flera år efter att vår apparat hade burits ut' - the room was still used afterwards. B killed on 'Samma soffgrupp står kvar hos honom.' D killed on 'Hos Hilding Wibbelund stod den i tre vintrar innan huset fick element'.
